ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r1.claim: Shahīq is a long, extended breath, from shāhiq meaning tall; al-Layth describes zafīr as a distressed full-chest breath and shahīq as its forceful exhalation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r1.anchor: والشهيق النفس الطويل الممتد، مأخوذ من قولهم: جبل شاهق أي طويل. وقال الليث: الزفير أن يملأ الرجل صدره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r5.claim: The Fire of the wretched is deprivation from what they sought and the pains of their sins, a punishment of the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r5.anchor: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار ) أي نار الحرمان عن المراد وآلام ما اكتسبوه من الآثام

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r1.claim: The majority read شقوا with fatḥa on shīn from intransitive شقي; al-Hasan reads damma and uses it transitively, meaning God made them wretched, like أشقاهم.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r1.anchor: الجمهور على فتح الشين لأنه من شقي فعل قاصر. وقرأ الحسن بضمها فاستعمله متعديا

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs read سعدوا with damma on sīn; the remaining readers have fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وحفص " سعدوا " بضم السين، والباقون بفتحها

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports that Hudhayl says سعده الله meaning أسعده.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r3.anchor: حكى الفراء عن هذيل أنها تقول

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r4.speaker: الجوهري
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r4.claim: Al-Jawhari gives سعد فهو سعيد like سلم فهو سليم, and سعد فهو مسعود.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r4.anchor: وقال الجوهري: " سعد فهو سعيد كسلم فهو سليم، وسعد فهو مسعود "

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r5.speaker: ابن القشيري
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qushayri reports سعده الله فهو مسعود and أسعد فهو مسعد.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r5.anchor: وقال ابن القشيري: " ورد سعده الله فهو مسعود، وأسعد فهو مسعد "

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r6.claim: Some say سعده and أسعده both occur and the triliteral passive مسعود supplants the augmented form.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r6.anchor: استغنوا باسم مفعول الثلاثي. وحكي عن الكسائي أنه قال

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r7.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi calls سعده and أسعده dialect variants meaning the same, فعل and أفعل.

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r8.claim: Abu Amr reports سعد الرجل as a form like جن; another report says سعده is a dialect.

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r9.speaker: المهدوي
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r9.claim: Al-Mahdawi weakens سعدوا: it must mean مسعود, an uncommon passive, since one says أسعده الله, not سعده الله.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r9.anchor: وقد ضعف جماعة قراءة الأخوين، قال المهدوي: من قرأ " سعدوا " فهو محمول على مسعود

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r10.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r10.claim: Al-Kisaʾi adduces مسعود; an objection says it may derive from مكان مسعود فيه with فيه deleted, so it does not prove سعده الله.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: احتج الكسائي بقولهم: " مسعود ". قيل: ولا حجة فيه، لأنه يقال: مكان مسعود فيه

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r11.speaker: علي بن سليمان
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r11.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman marvels that al-Kisaʾi read سعدوا despite his Arabic learning; the author finds Ali's astonishment itself astonishing.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r11.anchor: وكان علي بن سليمان يتعجب من قراءة الكسائي

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r12.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r12.claim: Makki calls the reading rare and anomalous: مسعود is analyzed as from أسعد الله with its augment removed, like مجنون as if from أجنه, although the simple verbs are not used.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r12.anchor: وقال مكي: " قراءة حمزة والكسائي " سعدوا " بضم السين

SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r13.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r13.claim: Most grammarians find the damma remote except by deleting augmentative letters; Abu al-Baqa says the form is neither attested in the language nor analogical.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106/r13.anchor: وضم السين بعيد عند أكثر النحويين إلا على حذف الزوائد. وقال أبو البقاء: " وهذا غير معروف في اللغة ولا هو مقيس "

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r1.claim: The clause may stand independently as an answer to an implied question, or be circumstantial, referring to the pronoun in ففي النار or to the Fire.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة فيها احتمالان، أحدهما: أنها مستأنفة، كأن سائلا سأل

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r2.claim: Zafir is a donkey’s first sound and shahiq its last; Ruʾbah’s verse uses شهق to describe the sound.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r2.anchor: والزفير: أول صوت الحمار، والشهيق: آخره، قال رؤبة

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r3.claim: Ibn Faris defines shahiq as opposite to zafir: shahiq draws breath inward, while zafir expels it from intense grief, linked to bearing a heavy load.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن فارس: " الشهيق ضد الزفير؛ لأن الشهيق رد النفس

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives a similar account and cites al-Shammakh’s line describing zafir followed by heaving shahiq.

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r5.claim: Another explanation takes shahiq as an extended breath, deriving it from شاهق, a tall mountain.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: الشهيق: النفس الممتد، مأخوذ من قولهم

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r6.speaker: الليث
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r6.claim: Al-Layth describes zafir as filling the chest with breath in severe distress and expelling it, then describes shahiq as expelling that breath.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r6.anchor: وقال الليث: " الزفير: أن يملأ الرجل صدره حال كونه في الغم الشديد

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliyah and al-Rabi ibn Anas place zafir in the throat and shahiq in the chest.
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس: " الزفير في الحلق والشهيق في الصدر

SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:106#2/r8.claim: A further view assigns zafir to a donkey and shahiq to a mule.

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r6.claim: Zafīr is a severe, ugly groan.

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r7.claim: Shahīq is a very severe, high-pitched groan.

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r8.speaker: أهل اللغة من البصريين والكوفيين
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r8.claim: Basran and Kufan linguists compare zafīr to the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahīq to its ending.
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r8.anchor: وزعم أهل اللغة من البصريين والكوفيين أن الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار في النهيق، والشهيق بمنزلة آخر صوته

ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.claim: A fourth view applies the exception to the mentioned groaning: they have it except for other kinds of punishment; likewise Paradise includes delights both mentioned and unmentioned, which Zajjaj says the unbroken gift supports.
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.anchor: وفيها قول رابع: أن الاستثناء وقع على أن لهم فيها زفيرا وشهيقا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p312#7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p312#7/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p312#7/r1.claim: Qatada says God knows the scope of the exception; he reports that some sinners are scorched by the Fire for their sins, then admitted to Paradise.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p312#7/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ إلا ما شاء ربك ﴾ قال الله أعلم بثنياه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r9.speaker: أهل اللغة من الكوفيين والبصريين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r9.claim: Kufan and Basran linguists say zafīr resembles the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahīq its end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r9.anchor: زعم أهل اللغة من الكوفيين والبصريين أن الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار، والشهيق بمنزلة آخر نهيقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r10.speaker: رؤبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r10.claim: Ruʾba's verse uses shahīq for the strained sound in the chest, illustrating the term.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r10.anchor: وقال رؤبة: حشرج في الصدر صهيلا وشهق ... حتى يقال ناهق وما نهق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r11.speaker: ابن فارس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r11.claim: Ibn Fāris says shahīq is the opposite of zafīr: inward breath, while zafīr is exhalation under the strain of running, from carrying a heavy load.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن فارس: الشهيق ضد الزفير، لأن الشهيق رد النفس، والزفير إخراج النفس من شدة الجري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r12.speaker: الشماخ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r12.claim: Al-Shammākh's line presents zafīr as the first sound, followed by a strained shahīq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p192#2/r12.anchor: وقال الشماخ: بعيد مدى التطريب أول صوته ... زفير ويتلوه شهيق محشرج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل والفراء وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil, and al-Farrāʾ, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, say zafīr is the start of a donkey's bray and shahīq its end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك ومقاتل والفراء: الزفير أول نهيق الحمار، والشهيق آخره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas place zafīr in the throat and shahīq in the chest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib says zafīr is a donkey's bray and shahīq a mule's.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن السائب: الزفير زفير الحمار، والشهيق شهيق البغال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.claim: Khālidīn is an accusative circumstantial expression denoting a state that is to come.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.anchor: وانتصاب خالدين على أنها حال مقدرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.claim: Mā is a temporal adverbial verbal noun, meaning for the duration that the heavens and earth endure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.anchor: وما مصدرية ظرفية أي: مدة دوام السموات والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.claim: The duration signifies perpetuity, like Arabic expressions “as long as Thabīr stands” or “as long as a star shines,” without regard to whether either lasts forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بهذا التوقيت التأييد كقول العرب: ما أقام ثبير وما لاح كوكب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.claim: Another view takes the heavens and earth as those of the afterlife, which endure forever; Quranic references support this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: سموات الآخرة وأرضها وهي دائمة لا بد، يدل على ذلك يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.claim: A view argues that the afterlife must include a heaven or other covering, since its inhabitants need something to shelter and shade them; whatever gives shade counts as a heaven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.anchor: ولأنه لا بد لأهل الآخرة مما يقلهم ويظلمهم، إما سماء يخلقها الله، أو يظلهم العرش وكلما أظلك فهو سماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heavens and earth return to their originating light and remain forever in the light of the Throne.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن السموات والأرض في الآخرة يردان إلى النور الذي أخذتا منه، فهما دائمتان أبدا في نور العرش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r12.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r12.claim: If the exception is from remaining forever in Hell, it can denote the time sinful believers spend there before leaving for Paradise; the damned then include unbelievers and sinful Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r12.anchor: وهذا روي معناه عن قتادة والضحاك وغيرهما، ويكون الذين شقوا شاملا للكفار وعصاة المسلمين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r1.claim: Those described as wretched are people for whom wretchedness has already been decreed, and they are settled in Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r1.anchor: فأما الذين شقوا ( أي سبقت لهم الشقاوة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة من الكوفية والبصرية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r2.claim: Kufan and Basran linguists compare zafir to the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahik to its final sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r2.anchor: قال أهل اللغة من الكوفية والبصرية : الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r3.speaker: رؤبة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r3.claim: Ru'ba's line describes a sound rising in the chest and a neigh or bray, illustrating the sound terms.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r3.anchor: قال رؤبة : حشرج في الصدر صهيلا أو شهق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r4.claim: Ibn Faris defines zafir as exhaling breath and shahik as drawing it back in.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : الزفير إخراج النفس والشهيق رده

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r5.speaker: الشماخ
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r5.claim: Al-Shammakh's line about a wild donkey illustrates zafir followed by shahik.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r5.anchor: قال الشماخ في حمار وحش : بعيد مدى التطريب أو صوته زفير

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r6.claim: Al-Raghib says zafir is repeated labored breathing that expands the ribs, related to carrying a heavy load; shahik is prolonged breath and its return.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r6.anchor: وقال الراغب : الزفير ترديد النفس حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r7.speaker: السائب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r7.claim: Al-Sa'ib unusually assigns zafir to donkeys and shahik to mules.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r7.anchor: وعن السائب أن الزفير للحمير والشهيق للبغال وهو غريب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r8.claim: The sounds convey anguish and grief, either picturing people overcome by heat and constricted breath or comparing their voices to donkeys.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r8.anchor: ويراد بهما الدلالة على كربهم وغمهم وتشبيه حالهم بحال من استولت على قلبه الحرارة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the sounds as regret, loud breathing, and uninterrupted weeping.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r9.anchor: والمأثور عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : يريد ندامة ونفسا عاليا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb with a damma on shin, using it transitively as in 'God made him wretched.'
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( شقوا ) بضم الشين فاستعمل متعديا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r11.claim: The sounds clause is either a fresh sentence answering an implied question about their condition or a circumstantial clause attached to Hell or its pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141#2/r11.anchor: وجملة ( لهم فيها زفير ) إلخ مستأنفة كأن سائلا قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines zafīr as a loud sound and shahīq as a faint sound.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: الزفير: الصوت الشديد، والشهيق الصوت الضعيف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r2.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil compare zafīr to the start of a donkey's braying and shahīq to its ending as the sound is drawn back into the belly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومقاتل: الزفير أول نهيق الحمار، والشهيق آخره إذا ردده في جوفه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya locates zafīr in the throat and shahīq in the chest.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200/r3.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: الزفير في الحلق والشهيق في الصدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r1.claim: Zafīr is exhaling breath and shahīq its return; both terms can denote either the start or end of a donkey’s bray.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r1.anchor: الزفير إخراج النفس والشهيق رده، واستعمالها في أول النهيق وآخره

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r2.claim: The paired sounds signify extreme anguish, like heat gripping the heart and trapping the breath within it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r2.anchor: والمراد بهما الدلالة على شدة كربهم وغمهم وتشبيه حالهم بمن استولت الحرارة على قلبه وانحصر فيه روحه

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r3.claim: Their cries may also be likened to the sounds of donkeys.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r4.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r4.claim: A reading pronounces شقوا with ḍamma on its initial consonant.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r1.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r1.claim: One reported analysis makes the exception apply to their groaning and gasping.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r1.anchor: وقيل هو من قوله: { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.claim: The wretched are mentioned first because most people perish and the passage is a warning, so the sequence begins with the group that makes the threat most forceful.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.anchor: بدأ تعالى بالأشقياء ترتيبا للنشر على ترتيب اللف

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.claim: The wretched are overcome by hardship and are judged to enter the Fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.anchor: { فأما الذين شقوا } أي أدركهم العسر والشدة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.claim: Al-Qamus glosses zafir as exhaling after drawing breath in, and shaheeq as sobbing that reverberates in the chest.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir explains zafir as the exit of their breaths and shaheeq as their breaths entering.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن كثير في تفسير سورة الأنبياء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says zafir is a loud sound; the segment breaks off before completing his gloss of shaheeq.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.claim: Al-Rummānī glosses zafīr as repeated voiced breathing and shahīq as a terrible prolonged inward sound; their roots suggest strain or length, while khālid means perpetual residence and dāʾim continuing duration.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الرماني : والزفير : ترديد النفس مع الصوت حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

BURSEVI:v4p119/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r1.claim: The wretched are those for whom misery was decreed and who were sentenced to the fire, where they reside.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r1.anchor: {فأما الذين شقوا} أي سبقت لهم الشقاوة وقضي لهم بالنار ففي النار أي مستقرون في جهنم

BURSEVI:v4p119/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r2.claim: Zafīr is forceful exhalation and shahīq its return or inhalation; the terms also name the beginning and end of a donkey's braying.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r2.anchor: الزفير إخراج النفس بقوة وشدة والشهيق رده واستعمالهما في أول ما ينهق الحمار وآخر ما يفرغ من نهيقه

BURSEVI:v4p119/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r3.claim: The verse explicitly likens their cries to donkeys' ugly sounds; the author compares them with the cries and bodily changes of people undergoing worldly torture, while saying the afterlife is far worse.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r3.anchor: وفيه استعارة تصريحية فإن المراد تشبيه صراخهم بأصوات الحمير

BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.claim: If the phrase means their coming to be in Hell, khālidīn is an anticipatory circumstantial from the pronoun implied in the locative's settlement clause.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.anchor: خالدين فيها مقيمين دائمين فيها حال مقدرة من ضمير الاستقرار في الظرف وهو قوله في النار هذا إن أريد حدوث كونهم في النار

BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.claim: Another grammatical view needs no anticipatory circumstantial: unlike 39:73, where permanence follows entry, the people here already abide in Hell.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا حاجة هنا إلى جعل الحال مقدرة كما في قوله تعالى : فادخلوها خالدين

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the wretched as major sinners from the Muslim community: punishment is temporary, intercession removes them, and the exception covers their time in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: هاتان من المخبآت قول الله {فمنهم شقي وسعيد}

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r1.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said some people will leave Hell, rejecting the Haruriyya’s claim.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يخرج قوم من النار ولا نقول كما قال أهل حروراء

DURR-FULL:v4p477/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says God’s later will abrogated the wretched people’s exception through 4:168, ending hope of release and establishing everlasting punishment.
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r3.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {فأما الذين شقوا} قال: فجاء بعد ذلك من مشيئة الله فنسخها فأنزل الله بالمدينة

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports ʿUmar’s view that even people of Hell who stayed as long as the dunes of ʿAlij would eventually leave.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.anchor: عن الحسن عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: لو لبث أهل النار في النار كقدر رمل عالج لكان لهم يوم

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra says a day will come when no one remains in Hell, and recites the verse about the wretched.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سيأتي على جهنم يوم لا يبقى فيها أحد وقرأ {فأما الذين شقوا} الآية

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.claim: Ibrahim says no Qur’anic verse gives greater hope to Hell’s inhabitants than this verse’s exception.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: ما في القرآن آية أرجى لأهل النار من هذه الآية {خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك}

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud says a time will come when Hell’s doors flutter.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ليأتين عليها زمانا تخفق أبوابها

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r7.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Hell is the faster of the two abodes to fill and to become desolate.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: حهنم أسرع الدارين عمرانا وأسرعهما خرابا

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines zafir as a loud throat sound and shahīq as a faint chest sound.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {لهم فيها زفير وشهيق} قال: الزفير الصوت الشديد في الحلق والشهيق الصوت الضعيف

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas compares zafir to a donkey’s bray in his answer to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله {لهم فيها زفير وشهيق} ما الزفير قال: زفير كزفير الحمار

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas calls these categories hidden matters and says grave sinners among the Muslim community may be punished in Hell, then released through believers' intercession and admitted to Paradise; they are called wretched while punished.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : هاتان من المخبيات فمنهم شقي وسعيد فهم قوم من اهل الكبائر من اهل هذه القبلة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two terms together denote a loud sound.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : لهم فيها زفير وشهيق يقول : صوت شديد

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r2.speaker: الضحاك، الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak, with a similar report from al-Rabi ibn Anas, says zafir is in the throat.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قوله : لهم فيها زفيرقال : الزفير في الحلق وروى عن الربيع بن انس مثل قول الضحاك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says shaheeq is a weak sound.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وشهيق قال صوت ضعيف

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says shaheeq is in the chest.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2085/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله : لهم فيها زفير وشهيققال : والشهيق في الصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r8.claim: Zafir is forceful exhalation under respiratory pressure; shahiq is its opposite, a strained drawing of air into the chest from urgent need to breathe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r8.anchor: والزفير : إخراج الأنفاس بدفع وشدة بسبب ضغط التنفس . والشهيق : عكسه وهو اجتلاب الهواء إلى الصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r9.claim: The verse singles out these disfiguring breaths to deter people from the causes of damnation; their ugliness frightens more than a bare mention of pain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r9.anchor: وخص بالذكر من أحوالهم في جهنم الزفير والشهيق تنفيرا من أسباب المصير إلى النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r1.claim: Depending on the exception at the end of verse 107, the wretched may be every punished person, unbelievers and sinners, or only those eternally punished, meaning unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r1.anchor: قوله: الذين شقوا على بعض التأويلات في الاستثناء الذي في آخر الآية يراد به كل من يعذب من كافر وعاص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r2.claim: Zafīr and shahīq are intense sounds associated with grief, pain, or torment, like a weeping person's cries.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r2.anchor: كما يفعل الباكي الذي يصيح خلال بكائه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls zafīr a sharp sound and shahīq a heavy one.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r4.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says zafīr comes from the chest and shahīq from the throat, while another view reverses them; Qatada compares them to a donkey's first and last brays.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو العالية «الزفير» من الصدر و «الشهيق» من الحلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers Abu al-ʿAliya's account: the chest and cavity expand in a zafra, while the final burst of voice and breath is a shahqa, as in a dying or unconscious person's gasp.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر ما قال أبو العالية: فإن الزفرة هي التي يعظم معها الصدر والجوف والشهقة هي الوقعة الأخيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r6.claim: Another derivation connects zafīr to zafr, severity, and shahīq to the word for a tall mountain, making them synonymous or close in meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207#2/r6.anchor: وقيل «الزفير» : مأخوذ من الزفر وهو الشدة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.speaker: أبو نضرة عن جابر أو أبي سعيد الخدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.claim: A report transmitted by Abū Naḍra from Jābir or Abū Saʿīd takes the exception from “in the Fire” as a delay before entry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.anchor: وهذا قول رواه أبو نضرة عن جابر أو عن أبي سعيد الخدري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that zafīr is like the donkey’s initial bray from the chest, while shahīq is its final bray from the throat; al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil, and al-Farrāʾ agree. Al-Zajjāj instead glosses them as severe, ugly groaning and very high, intense groaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r1.anchor: أن الزفير كزفير الحمار في الصدر وهو أول ما ينهق والشهيق كشهيق الحمار في الحلق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r2.claim: In a report from Ibn ʿAbbās through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, zafīr is in the throat and shahīq in the chest; Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas also hold this ordering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r2.anchor: أن الزفير في الحلق والشهيق في الصدور رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r3.claim: A different report from Ibn ʿAbbās defines zafīr as a loud sound and shahīq as a weak sound.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r3.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس الزفير الصوت الشديد والشهيق الصوت الضعيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r4.claim: Ibn Fāris says shahīq is the opposite of zafīr: shahīq draws breath inward and zafīr expels it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن فارس الشهيق ضد الزفير لأن الشهيق رد النفس والزفير إخراج النفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r5.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r5.claim: Other linguists derive zafīr from carrying a heavy burden and shahīq from a long, extended breath, comparing it with a tall mountain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r5.anchor: وقال غيره الزفير الشديد مأخوذ من الزفر وهو الحمل على الظهر لشدته والشهيق النفس الطويل الممتد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r6.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib says zafīr is the donkey’s sound and shahīq the mule’s sound.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#3/r6.anchor: والثالث أن الزفير زفير الحمار والشهيق شهيق البغال قاله ابن السائب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p351/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p351/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p351/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the zafir is in the throat and the shahiq in the chest: their exhalation and inhalation reflect their torment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p351/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر أي: تنفسهم زفير

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r5.claim: Zafīr is repeated breathing with sound and grief until the ribs swell; its root connotes intensity, with related uses for heavy loads, binding, a roaring fire, and water carriers.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r5.anchor: الزفير: ترديد النفس مع الصوت مع الحزن

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r6.claim: One account reverses the breath terms: shahiq is drawing breath back in and zafīr is breathing it out.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r6.anchor: وقيل: الزفير الشهيق؛ لأن الشهيق رد النفس

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r7.claim: Ali ibn Isa describes shahiq as a dreadful deep sound during extended breathing; its root suggests excessive length, as in جبل شاهق.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r7.anchor: عن علي بن عيسى، وأصله: الطول المفرط

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r8.claim: Another distinction makes zafīr the first donkey bray and shahiq its last.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r8.anchor: وقيل: الزفير: أول نهاق الحمير، والشهيق: آخر نهاقها

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r9.speaker: ابن عرفة
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r9.claim: Ibn Arafa says zafīr comes from the chest and shahiq from the throat; both are sounds of sufferers.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r9.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: والزفير من الصدر، والشهيق من الحلق

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r5.claim: After saying that people are wretched or happy, the passage describes each group's state; the wretched enter Hell deserving punishment as recompense for their deeds.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r5.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر القيامة، وأن منهم شقي وسعيد، بين حال كل واحد

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says zafīr is the loud sound and shahiq the weak sound.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r6.anchor: الصوت الشديد، والشهيق: الصوت الضعيف، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r7.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r7.claim: Muqatil and al-Dahhak say zafīr is the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahiq its last sound as it ends and echoes in its throat.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل والضحاك. قال قتادة: صوت الكافر في النار

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r8.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r8.claim: Qatada compares the disbeliever's voice in Hell to a donkey's: it begins with zafīr and ends with shahiq.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: صوت الكافر في النار صوت الحمار

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliya locates zafīr in the throat and shahiq in the chest.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r9.anchor: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر، عن أبي العالية

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r10.claim: Other explanations take the sounds as cries of woe or continual weeping from the severity of their plight, the latter reported by the Qadi.

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r9.claim: Every wretched person is in Hell, including a sinner, contrary to the Murji'a.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r9.anchor: وتدل على أن كل شقي في النار وإن كان فاسقا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r1.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on the shīn; al-Ḥasan reads it with ḍamma, matching ‘saʿidū.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r1.anchor: وعن الحسن ( شقوا ) بالضم ، كما قرىء :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r2.claim: Zafīr is breathing out and shahīq is drawing the breath back in.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r3.speaker: الشماخ
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r3.claim: Al-Shammākh’s verse uses ‘zafīr’ followed by ‘shahīq’ to witness the contrast between exhalation and inhalation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r3.anchor: قال الشماخ : بعيد مدى التطريب أول صوته … زفير ويتلوه شهيق محشرج

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says zafīr is a loud sound and shahīq a faint one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r1.anchor: أن الزفير الصوت الشديد , والشهيق الصوت الضعيف , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas locates zafīr in the throat from intense grief and shahīq in the chest.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r2.anchor: والشهيق في الصدر , قاله الربيع بن أنس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r3.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says zafīr is repeated breathing from grief, linked to bearing a load, while shahīq is an extended breath, linked to a tall mountain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r3.anchor: مأخوذ من قولهم جبل شاهق أي طويل , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r4.claim: A fourth gloss compares zafīr to a donkey's first bray and shahīq to its last; the cited line depicts the sounds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p504/r4.anchor: حشرج في الجوف سحيلا أو شهق

MUQATIL:11:106-107/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:106-107/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:106-107/r1.claim: Zafir is like a donkey's final bray and shaheeq like its first; Abu al-Abbas Thaʿlab says zafir comes from the whole body and shaheeq from the chest.

MUQATIL:11:106-107/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:106-107/r2.speaker: أبو العباس ثعلب
MUQATIL:11:106-107/r2.claim: Abu al-Abbas Thaʿlab distinguishes them by saying zafir comes from the whole body and shaheeq from the chest.
MUQATIL:11:106-107/r2.anchor: قال أبو العباس ثعلب: الزفير من البدن كله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r1.claim: Zafīr is the donkey's first bray and shahīq its last; alternatively, they are the expelling and drawing back of breath.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r1.anchor: هو أول نهيق الحمار ﴿ وشهيق ﴾ هو آخره أو هما إخراج النفس ورده

NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r2.claim: The clause is circumstantial, governed by the implicit existential in fī al-nār.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#3/r2.anchor: والجملة فى موضع الحال والعامل فيها الاستقرار الذى فى النار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that the exception in both verses concerns Paradise's people: sinful Muslims do not remain eternally in Hell, and do not remain eternally in Paradise without having entered it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.anchor: عن أبى هريرة رضى الله عنه عن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال الاستثناء فى الآيتين لأهل الجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.claim: The Muʿtazila reject the transmitted reports because they deny that sinners leave Hell; the author calls this a manifest sin.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.anchor: والمعتزلة لما لم يروا خروج العصاة من النار ردوا الأحاديث المروية فى هذا الباب وكفى به اثما مبينا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r3.claim: Fa-ammā alladhīna shaqū begins a subject phrase; fī al-nār is its predicate, as is lahum fīhā zafīr wa-shahīq.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r3.anchor: { فأما الذين شقوا } ابتداء. { ففي النار } في موضع الخبر، وكذا { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya first says zafīr comes from the chest and shahīq from the throat.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r4.anchor: قال أبو العالية: الزفير من الصدر، والشهيق من الحلق

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya also transmits the reverse assignment of the two sounds to chest and throat.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines zafīr as a groan from severe pain and shahīq as an extremely loud groan.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الزفير من شدة الأنين، والشهيق من الأنين المرتفع جدا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r7.speaker: أهل اللغة من الكوفيين والبصريين
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r7.claim: Kufan and Basran linguists compare zafīr to the beginning of a donkey’s bray and shahīq to its ending.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r7.anchor: وزعم أهل اللغة من الكوفيين والبصريين أن الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمير في النهيق

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reverses the comparison: zafīr is the loud sound, shahīq the weak one.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه عكسه قال: الزفير الصوت الشديد، والشهيق الصوت الضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r9.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil say zafīr is like the first bray of a donkey and shahīq its final sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومقاتل: الزفير مثل أول نهيق الحمار، والشهيق مثل آخره حين فرغ من صوته

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r10.claim: The cited poetic line describes a breath or groan that can be heard as a bray, bearing on the meaning of shahīq.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r10.anchor: قال الشاعر: حشرج في الجوف سحيلا أو شهق حتى يقال ناهق وما نهق

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r11.claim: One view defines zafīr as breathing out when grief fills the chest, and shahīq as drawing the breath back in.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r11.anchor: وقيل: الزفير إخراج النفس، وهو أن يمتلىء الجوف غما فيخرج بالنفس، والشهيق رد النفس

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r12.claim: Another view derives zafīr from a heavy load and calls it repeated breathing from grief; shahīq is a long, extended breath, like a lofty mountain.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r12.anchor: وقيل: الزفير ترديد النفس من شدة الحزن مأخوذ من الزفر وهو الحمل على الظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r13.claim: Both zafīr and shahīq are sounds made by people in grief.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r7.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وأبو سنان
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r7.claim: Al-Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abū Sinān, and others take the wretched to include sinful believers; the exception from “abiding” means they are taken from Hell after a period.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r7.anchor: قاله قتادة والضحاك وأبو سنان وغيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī takes the exception from the mentioned sounds and blessings: those in Hell also receive unmentioned kinds of punishment, and the people of Paradise unmentioned kinds of bliss.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108/r9.anchor: الثالث: أن الاستثناء من الزفير والشهيق أي لهم فيها زفير وشهيق إلا ما شاء ربك من أنواع العذاب

QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.claim: Fire signifies the self’s punishment through deprivation and painful states; the garden signifies its reward through attaining desires and pleasures.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.anchor: المراد بالنار والجنة عذاب النفس بنار الحرمان عن المراد وآلام الهيئات والآثار وثواب النفس بجنة حصول المرادات واللذات

QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.claim: On the outwardly careful reading, the wretched leave that fire only for worse fires of the heart and spirit, while the blessed move to greater gardens of the heart’s divine disclosure and the spirit’s encounter with God.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.anchor: خروج الشقي منها إلى ما هو أشد منه من نيران القلب

QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.claim: The blessed cannot leave paradise for fire; the unsevered gift supports the permanence of their state and, by opposition, the permanence of the wretched person’s punishment, while the threat in 11:107 is severe.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.anchor: لكون الشقي في مقابلة السعيد وخروج السعيد من الجنة إلى النار محال

QASHANI:11:105-108/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r5.claim: In the deeper account, the wretched remain in fire but move between its levels; with God holding his forelock on a straight path, his own desire drives him to hell, where he enjoys what suits him and the fire becomes pleasure.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r5.anchor: وأما الحقيقة فتحكم بأن الشقي لما كان في المراتب المذكورة

QASHANI:11:105-108/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r6.claim: The commentary cites an unattributed hadith that watercress will grow at the bottom of hell.

QASHANI:11:105-108/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r7.claim: It also cites an unattributed hadith saying a time will come when hell claps its doors and has no one inside.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r7.anchor: يأتي على جهنم زمان يصفق أبوابها ليس فيها أحد

QASHANI:11:105-108/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r9.claim: If the indefinite nouns indicate kinds rather than exaltation, the wretched may leave for paradise by purifying the soul of dark traits and sin’s consequences, and would not then be wretched forever.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r9.anchor: وإن جعل التنكير في قوله: { شقي وسعيد } للنوعية لا للتعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r2.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r2.claim: Al-Layth distinguishes zafir as drawing a breath into the chest in grief without expelling it, and shahiq as releasing that breath.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r2.anchor: قال الليث : الزفير أن يملأ الرجل صدره حال كونه في الغم الشديد من النفس ولم يخرجه ، والشهيق أن يخرج ذلك النفس

RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ notes that a horse may be called great in zafra, meaning large-bellied.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : يقال للفرس إنه عظيم الزفرة أي عظيم البطن

RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r4.claim: Al-Razi explains physiologically: grief traps the heart’s spirit and intensifies heat; one draws much cool air, swelling the chest, then struggles to expel it. In physicians’ usage inhalation is zafir and exhalation shahiq; both signal anguish.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r4.anchor: فعلى قياس قول الأطباء الزفير هو استدخال الهواء الكثير

RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r5.claim: Some distinguish zafir as the beginning of a donkey’s bray and shahiq as its final sound.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار بالنهيق . وأما الشهيق فهو بمنزلة آخر صوت الحمار

RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says zafir is ascent: Hell’s flames lift the damned until they hope to escape, then angels strike them with iron maces and return them to the lowest level; descent is shahiq.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r6.anchor: قال الحسن : قد ذكرنا أن الزفير عبارة عن الارتفاع . فنقول : الزفير لهيب جهنم يرفعهم بقوته

RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.claim: Abu Muslim says zafir is breath gathering in the chest during intense sobbing and interrupting respiration; shahiq appears with acute distress and grief, possibly followed by fainting or death.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : الزفير ما يجتمع في الصدر من النفس عند البكاء الشديد

RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya places zafir in the throat and shahiq in the chest.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.anchor: الوجه الخامس : قال أبو العالية : الزفير في الحلق والشهيق في الصدر .

RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.claim: Another group says zafir is a loud sound and shahiq a quiet one.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.anchor: الوجه السادس : قال قوم : الزفير الصوت الشديد ، والشهيق الصوت الضعيف .

RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the words as regret, a loud breath, unceasing weeping, and grief that cannot be dispelled.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق } يريد ندامة ونفسا عالية وبكاء لا ينقطع

RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi says zafir suggests strength and shahiq weakness according to the language.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r5.anchor: الوجه الثامن : الزفير مشعر بالقوة ، والشهيق بالضعف

RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi offers a spiritual reading: zafir suggests strong attachment to worldly pleasures, while shahiq suggests inability to attain spiritual bliss and divine lights.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50#2/r6.anchor: إذا عرفت هذا فنقول : لم يبعد أن يكون المراد من الزفير قوة ميلهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.claim: Another proposal attaches the exception to their sighing and gasping: once they become motionless, that combined condition ceases even though they remain in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.anchor: الوجه الرابع : في الجواب قالوا : الاستثناء يرجع إلى قوله

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.claim: Some scholars say the exception removes monotheist sinners from Hell's everlasting sentence: since unbelievers remain forever, those exempted from that rule are sinful Muslims; Razi calls this a strong argument.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.anchor: الوجه السادس : في الجواب قال قوم : هذا الاستثناء يفيد إخراج أهل التوحيد من النار

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.claim: He rejects attaching the exception to sighing and gasping as another departure from the apparent meaning.

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r1.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r1.claim: When souls are given divine success, abandonment cannot reach them; when hearts attain realization, deprivation has no path to them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r1.anchor: وقيل إذا أخذ النفوس بالتوفيق فلا سبيل للخذلان إليها ، وإذا أخذ القلوب بالتحقيق فلا طريق للحرمان عليها

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r3.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r3.claim: Yesterday is gone, tomorrow is only hoped for, and today is the witnessed moment that may vanish, so it should be used for what benefits.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r3.anchor: ويقال الأيام ثلاثة : يوم مفقود وهو أمس ليس بيدك منه شيء ، ويوم مقصود وهو غد لا تدري أتدركه أم لا

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r4.claim: Lifespans proceed according to God’s knowledge and will; effort cannot advance or delay death once its appointed time arrives.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r4.anchor: والآجال على ما علمها الحق - سبحانه - وأرادها جارية ؛ فلا طلب يقدم أو يؤخر وقتا إذا جاء أجله

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r5.claim: Union and arrival also have appointed times, so neither hoping to arrive nor fearing loss can change their time.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r5.anchor: وكذلك للوصول وقت ، فلا طلب مع رجاء الوصول ، ولا طلب مع خوف الزوال

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r6.claim: A poem calls safety defective because it leaves its possessor expecting calamity, while trial is valuable because joy may follow it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r6.anchor: ولقد قيل : عيب السلامة أن صاحبها . . . متوقع لقواصم الظهر وفضيلة البلوى ترقب أهلها . . . عقب البلاء - مسرة الدهر

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r7.claim: The wretched are those allotted deprivation in their present state; the blessed are those granted faith in their final state.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r7.anchor: الشقي من قسم له الحرمان في حاله

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r8.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r8.claim: Misery, and likewise happiness, may be temporary or enduring.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r8.anchor: ويقال الشقاء على قسمين : قوم شقاؤهم غير مؤيد ، وقوم شقاؤهم على التأييد وكذلك القول في السعادة

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r9.claim: The spiritually wretched are bound to their own management and forget divine decree; the happy turn from planning’s darkness to witnessing decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r9.anchor: الشقي من هو في أسر التدبير ونسيان جريان التقدير

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r10.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r10.claim: The wretched think their obedience comes from themselves, whereas the happy know that all events belong to God and are free of the ego’s bondage.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r10.anchor: ويقال الشقي من كان في رق العبودية ظانا أن منه طاعاته ، السعيد من تحرر عن رق البشرية وعلم أن الحادثات كلها لله

QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r11.claim: Those eternally wretched are the people of Hell under the threat, while the eternally happy are those promised whatever they wish and more.
QUSHAYRI:v2p58/r11.anchor: وأما الأشقياء - على التأبيد - فهم أهل الخلود في مقتضى الوعيد ، والسعداء - على التأبيد - من قال الله تعالى في صفتهم

STUDYQURAN:11:106/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r1.claim: Hell's groaning and wailing describe heavy breathing, ceaseless weeping, and extreme pain, regret, and incurable grief.
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r1.anchor: which means that they will be breathing heavily, weeping ceaselessly, and experiencing an extreme state of pain, regret, and incurable grief (R).

STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.speaker: al-Bayḍāwī
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī says the heavens and earth enduring refers to the Afterlife's basic topographic setting, not serial time or physical-world time; 14:48 depicts the earth and heavens changed on that Day.
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.anchor: Bayḍāwī argues that the period in Hell described as for so long as

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r8.claim: Zafīr is the first sound of a donkey's braying and similar sounds.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r8.anchor: لهم، وهو أول نهاق الحمار وشبهه

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r9.claim: Shahīq is the final bray, echoed in the animal's chest; Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj's line uses “shahiq” for that sound.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r9.anchor: وشهيق} [هود: 106] وهو آخر نهيقه إذا ردده في الجوف عند فراغه من نهاقه، كما قال رؤبة بن العجاج: [البحر الرجز] حشرج في الجوف سحيلا أو شهق

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the two sounds as a loud sound and a faint sound.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {لهم فيها زفير وشهيق} [هود: 106] يقول: صوت شديد وصوت ضعيف "

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r11.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r11.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says zafīr is in the throat and shahīq in the chest.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي العالية، في قوله: " {لهم فيها زفير وشهيق} [هود: 106] قال: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر "

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r12.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r12.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas also transmits Abū al-ʿĀliya's explanation that zafīr is in the throat and shahīq in the chest.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r12.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية بنحوه

TAB-FULL:v12p578/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p578/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p578/r1.claim: Qatāda says the disbeliever's voice in Hell is like a donkey: zafīr first, then shahīq.
TAB-FULL:v12p578/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «صوت الكافر في النار صوت الحمار، أوله زفير وآخره شهيق»

TAB-FULL:v12p580/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r1.claim: Qatāda says God knows what His exception means, and reports that people scorched by Hell for their sins will later enter Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r1.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، في قوله: " {فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: الله أعلم بثنياه

TAB-FULL:v12p580/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r3.claim: Anas reports from the Prophet that a group will come out of Hell.
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r3.anchor: ثنا أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «يخرج قوم من النار»

TAB-FULL:v12p580/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r6.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says some people will leave Hell for Paradise; they are those covered by the exception.
TAB-FULL:v12p580/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، " {فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار} [هود: 106] إلى قوله: {خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك}

TAB-FULL:v12p582/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p582/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p582/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the exception for monotheist sinners who enter Hell and remain there for a time before being brought to Paradise. Polytheists are promised eternal Hell, while transmitted reports say sinful believers are removed; the alternative would contradict scholarly doctrine and reports by denying that sinners enter Paradise or believers enter Hell.
TAB-FULL:v12p582/r7.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال في تأويل هذه الآية بالصواب، القول الذي ذكرنا عن قتادة والضحاك، من أن ذلك استثناء في أهل التوحيد

TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.claim: The questioning and intermediate reward or punishment in individual graves differ from the final accounting and decisive, everlasting reward of the Resurrection; barzakh questioning completes the record for Judgment Day, while its garden or fire is only a preliminary lodging.
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.anchor: فإن الذي يستقبل الإنسان في البرزخ هو المسألة لتكميل صحيفة أعماله ليدخر لفصل القضاء يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:11:100-108/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r3.claim: The Pharaoh verses distinguish being shown the Fire before the Hour from entering it afterward, and being dragged through boiling water before being kindled in Hell, marking barzakh punishment as preliminary.
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r3.anchor: فترى الآية تعبر عن عذابهم بالعرض على النار ثم يوم القيامة بدخولها وهو أشد العذاب

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r1.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r1.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses zafīr as the donkey's first bray and shahīq as its last bray.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r1.anchor: قال في المجمع الزفير أول نهاق الحمار والشهيق آخر نهاقه

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's al-Kashshāf defines zafīr as breathing out and shahīq as drawing the breath back in.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r2.anchor: وقال في الكشاف الزفير إخراج النفس والشهيق رده

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines zafīr as repeated breathing until the ribs swell; shahīq is prolonged zafīr and its return, while zafīr is its extension.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r3.anchor: وقال الراغب في المفردات، الزفير تردد النفس حتى ينتفخ الضلوع منه

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r4.claim: The senses are close, and the wording is metaphorical: the damned draw breath into their chests then expel it with loud crying and groaning from the fire's pain, like a braying donkey.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r4.anchor: والمعاني - كما ترى - متقاربة وكان في الكلام استعارة

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.claim: The collective context of the Day of Gathering favors plural wording; the preceding universal negation uses singular indefinite nafs, then the passage returns to the plural for the two groups.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.anchor: ومقتضاها المضي على هيئة الجمع الذين شقوا والذين سعدوا

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.claim: The clause describes the duration of Hell's inhabitants, just as the next verse describes the Garden's inhabitants, confirming their settled residence.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.anchor: بيان لمكث أهل النار فيها كما أن الآية التالية

TABATABAI:11:108/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري وجماعة من التابعين
TABATABAI:11:108/r3.claim: A sixth view identifies the wretched as sinful monotheists who enter Hell, then leave for Paradise; the exception covers their release and the happy group's prior time in Hell, so the same people are wretched there and happy in Paradise.
TABATABAI:11:108/r3.anchor: ونسبوا هذا القول إلى ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبي سعيد الخدري من الصحابة وجماعة من التابعين

TABATABAI:11:108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.claim: The context divides all people gathered for Judgment into two groups, and the clauses beginning with أما explain those same exhaustive groups; they cannot mean only selected sinners and former sinners.
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.anchor: مبدوين بأما التفصيلية مسوقان لتفصيل ما أجمل في قوله

TABATABAI:11:108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.claim: Recasting the initial division as a special group leaves the general context unexplained and makes the doubled subjects, durations, and exceptions confusing and needlessly complex.
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.anchor: السياق الظاهر في وصف أهل الجمع عامة لا يساعد على إرادة طائفة خاصة منهم

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī formulates the extraction view generally: all the gathered divide into Hell's wretched and Paradise's happy, while both exceptions concern sinful monotheists removed from Hell to Paradise; this avoids most earlier objections.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يقرر هذا الوجه على وجه التعميم بأن يقال المراد

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.claim: A seventh view says the will clause reinforces endless abiding: God will never will their departure, so the exception does not shorten their stay; it protects permanence from any cause except God's will.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.anchor: إن التعليق بالمشيئة إنما هو على سبيل التأكيد للخلود والتبعيد للخروج لأن الله سبحانه لا يشاء إلا خلودهم على ما حكم به

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.speaker: سلام بن المستنير البصري
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.claim: An eighth view makes the exception the time difference between successive groups entering Hell or Paradise, as groups are led in procession.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.anchor: ونقل الوجه عن سلام بن المستنير البصري

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.claim: The wording describes the duration of residence by its endpoint, not its start; everyone begins settling in Hell or Paradise on Judgment Day, so staggered arrivals do not explain the exception.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.anchor: أن الوصف ناظر إلى مدة الكون في النار أو الجنة من جهة النهاية

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.claim: A ninth view says the wretched remain in Hell during the world's duration, including their time in graves; when heaven and earth end, their torment pauses until resurrection, which is the exception.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.anchor: نقله في مجمع البيان عن شيخنا أبي جعفر الطوسي في تفسيره ناقلا عن جمع من أصحابنا في تفاسيرهم

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the ninth view restates the second view's reading of illa as 'other than' and inherits the objections raised against it.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.anchor: وفيه إن مرجعه إلى الوجه الثاني المبني على أخذ

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r2.claim: A tenth view makes the first exception exclude people God pardons before they enter Hell; the Paradise exception then excludes sinful monotheists who enter Hell and later reach Paradise.

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.claim: The proposed account fits only the first exception and requires a different explanation for the second, breaking the two verses' contextual unity.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.anchor: وفيه إن ما ذكره إنما يجري في أول الاستثناءين

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.claim: People God pardons are not arbitrarily excused: pardon rests on a good deed or intercession, making them happy from the outset and included in Paradise's group, not wretches who must be excepted.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.anchor: هم ليسوا بأشقياء حتى يستثنوا بل سعداء داخلون في الجنة من أول

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r7.claim: Qatada recited 11:106 and reported from Anas that the Prophet said a group will emerge from Hell.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، أنه تلا هذه الآية

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r8.claim: Qatada added that they do not say what the people of Haruraʾ say; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī identifies the Harurites as Kharijites who claim whoever enters Hell remains there forever.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r8.anchor: ولا نقول كما قال أهل حروراء

TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.claim: Jabir reports that after reciting the wretched people's passage through the exception, the Prophet said that if God wills to take some of them from Hell and put them in Paradise, He can.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.anchor: إن شاء الله أن يخرج أناسا من الذين شقوا من النار فيدخلهم الجنة فعل

TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r2.claim: In al-Burhan, Muhammad ibn Muslim asks Imam al-Sadiq about the Jahannamiyyun; Abu Jaʿfar says they leave Hell, reach the spring of life at Paradise's gate, and regrow after its water is sprinkled on them. A parallel transmission comes through ʿUmar ibn Aban.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن الجهنميين فقال كان أبو جعفر يقول يخرجون منها

TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.claim: Jahannamiyyun are a particular group of Hell's inhabitants: monotheists released through intercession, not all who enter Hell.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.anchor: والمراد بالجهنميين طائفة خاصة من أهل النار وهم أهل التوحيد الخارجون منها بالشفاعة

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar tells Abu Basir that some become charcoal in Hell before intercession takes them to a river from Paradise's spring; bathing restores their flesh and removes the fire's grime, and Paradise's people call them Jahannamiyyun until God removes that name.
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r1.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول إن أناسا يخرجون من النار

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the enemies of ʿAli remain in Hell forever and intercession does not reach them.
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r2.anchor: يا أبا بصير إن أعداء علي هم المخلدون في النار ولا تدركهم الشفاعة

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r3.speaker: عبد صالح
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r3.claim: A righteous servant says Jahannamiyyun enter Hell for their sins and leave through God's pardon.
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r3.anchor: قال سمعت عبدا صالحا يقول في الجهنميين إنهم يدخلون النار بذنوبهم

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.speaker: السدي
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says both clauses were later abrogated: a Medinan threat removed hope that Hell's people would leave, while a promise to believers established Paradise's eternal duration.
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ عن السدي في قوله

TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects al-Suddi's abrogation claim: it assumes the verses imply eventual termination, lacks rational or transmitted basis, conflicts with explicit Paradise wording, and ignores other Meccan declarations of both groups' abiding.
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.anchor: ما ذكره من نسخ الآيتين زعما منه أنهما تدلان على الانقطاع

TABATABAI:11:108#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r2.claim: Hasan reports that ʿUmar said that even if Hell's people stayed as long as a heap of sand at ʿAlij, a day would come when they left.
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r2.anchor: عن الحسن عن عمر قال لو لبث أهل النار في النار كقدر رمل عالج لكان لهم يوم على ذلك يخرجون فيه

TABATABAI:11:108#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra says a day will come when no one remains in Hell, and he recited 11:106.
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال سيأتي على جهنم يوم لا يبقى فيها أحد

TABATABAI:11:108#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r5.claim: Ibrahim also attributes to Ibn Masʿud the claim that a time will come when Hell's doors flap with no one left inside.
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r5.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ليأتين عليها زمان تخفق أبوابها

TABATABAI:11:108#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r8.claim: Many reports from the Imami Imams establish disbelievers' eternal punishment; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī previously discussed whether punishment can end in his commentary on 2:167.
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r8.anchor: والروايات الدالة على خلود الكفار في النار من طرق أئمة أهل البيت كثيرة جدا

TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.claim: شقاء, شقاوة, and شقوة mean the same; the yāʾ in شقي comes from wāw, and saʿāda is the opposite of misery.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.anchor: الشقاء والشقاوة والشقوة بمعنى والياء في شقي

TABRISI:11:104-108/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r4.claim: Zafīr is the beginning of a donkey’s bray and breath repeatedly sounded from grief until the ribs swell; related usage also conveys intensity, burden, mastery, or the sound of fire.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r4.anchor: والزفير أول نهاق الحمار والشهيق آخر نهاقه قال رؤبة

TABRISI:11:104-108/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r5.claim: Zafīr is breath repeated with sound from grief until the ribs swell.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r5.anchor: والزفير ترديد النفس مع الصوت من الحزن حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

TABRISI:11:104-108/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r6.claim: Shahīq is the dreadful sound drawn from the innermost body with a prolonged breath; its root suggests excessive height or length.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r6.anchor: والشهيق صوت فظيع يخرج من الجوف بمد النفس

TABRISI:11:106-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:106-108/r1.claim: The wretched are in the Fire as punishment for evil deeds; they are called wretched before entry because their present state leads to it.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r1.anchor: يعني أن الذين شقوا باستحقاقهم العذاب

TABRISI:11:106-108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r2.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:11:106-108/r2.claim: The Prophet’s saying “the wretched one is wretched in his mother’s womb” means the person is known to become wretched through evil deeds leading to Hell, like an old father’s son called an orphan because he will be orphaned.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r2.anchor: ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:11:106-108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:106-108/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says these are sounds of distressed, grieving people: zafīr is a harsh beginning of a groan and shahīq a very loud, intense groan like the end of a donkey’s bray.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: الزفير والشهيق من أصوات المكروبين

TABRISI:11:106-108/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:106-108/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the sounds as remorse, a high breath, and unceasing weeping.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: يريد ندامة ونفسا عاليا

TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.speaker: الضحاك والجبائي
TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Jubbāʾī take this literally of the transformed skies and earth of the Hereafter, which will not perish when recreated after annihilation.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.anchor: أن المراد ما دامت السماوات والأرض مبدلتين

TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.claim: Another view means the skies and earth of Paradise and Hell: everything above is sky and everything under one’s feet is earth; this is close to the first view.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.anchor: أن المراد ما دامت سماوات الجنة والنار وأرضهما

TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase means the Hereafter, which lasts forever, just as the world’s skies and earth endured for the duration of its construction.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.anchor: وهي دائمة أبدا كما أن دوام السماء والأرض في الدنيا قدر مدة بنائها عن الحسن

TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.claim: The phrase is an Arabic idiom of perpetuity, not a literal time limit: formulas about night and day, sky and earth, and other supposedly unchanging things mean forever.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.anchor: ألفاظا للتبعيد في معنى التأبيد يقولون لا أفعل ذلك ما اختلف الليل والنهار

TABRISI:11:106-108/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r9.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
TABRISI:11:106-108/r9.claim: Poetry by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib uses the two unsetting stars as an image of enduring permanence; Zuhayr similarly speaks of mountains, sky, stars, and lasting days.

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج والفراء وعلي بن عيسى
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.claim: One view makes the exception an increase beyond the stated span: extra punishment for Hell’s people or bliss for Paradise’s; here إلا means سوى, “apart from.”
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.anchor: أنه استثناء في الزيادة من العذاب لأهل النار

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.speaker: المازني والبلخي
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.claim: Another view applies the exception to time spent at the gathering and judgment or in the barzakh; al-Balkhī prefers this explanation.
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.anchor: أن الاستثناء واقع على مقامهم في المحشر والحساب

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the Hell exception attaches to kinds of torment beyond the two sounds, and the Paradise exception to kinds of bliss; neither limits eternal duration.
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.anchor: أن الاستثناء الأول يتصل بقوله { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
