TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes إلا to mean “and,” adding whatever God wills; grammarians versed in the language weakened this analysis.
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.anchor: أن يكون إلا بمعنى الواو أي وما شاء ربك من الزيادة عن الفراء

TABRISI:11:107-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:107-108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:107-108/r1.claim: The cited poem describes a vanished house whose remaining cold ashes are guarded from wind; al-Farrāʾ reads إلا there as “and.”

TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.claim: The author selects the interpretation that sinful monotheists may be released from Hell and brought to Paradise, with a corresponding time exception in the Paradise verse.
TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.anchor: وهذا القول هو المختار المعول عليه

FARRA:v2p27/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p27/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p27/r2.claim: Zafīr is the beginning of a donkey’s bray, and shahīq is its end.
FARRA:v2p27/r2.anchor: فالزفير أول نهيق الحمار وشبهه، والشهيق من آخره.

THALABI:v5p188/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p188/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas defines zafīr as a loud sound and shahīq as a faint sound.
THALABI:v5p188/r14.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الزفير: الصوت الشديد، والشهيق: الصوت الضعيف

THALABI:v5p188/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r15.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
THALABI:v5p188/r15.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil compare zafīr to a donkey's first bray and shahīq to its final sound as it draws the sound back into its body.
THALABI:v5p188/r15.anchor: الضحاك ومقاتل: الزفير: أول نهيق الحمار، والشهيق آخره حين يفرغ من صوته

THALABI:v5p188/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r16.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v5p188/r16.claim: Abu al-Aliyah places zafīr in the throat and shahīq in the chest.
THALABI:v5p188/r16.anchor: أبو العالية: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r1.claim: Al-Layth defines zafīr as expelling breath and shahīq as drawing breath back in; the other lexicographers likewise describe the breath cycle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r1.anchor: قال الليث (¬5): الزفر والزفير أن يملأ الرجل صدره غما ثم هو يزفر به، فالزفير إخراج النفس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r2.speaker: الجعدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r2.claim: Al-Jaʿdī's horse poem uses zafra for a horse with a large belly, as though it were always exhaling and had been formed in that state.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r2.anchor: وأنشد للجعدي (¬1): خيط على زفرة فتم ولم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt explains al-Rāʿī's mare as folded over its breaths like arches that have settled, illustrating the word's bodily sense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq says both are sounds made by people overwhelmed with distress and grief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق (¬4): هما من أصوات المكروبين المحزونين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r5.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil compare zafīr to the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahīq to its end as the sound is drawn back into the throat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r5.anchor: الضحاك (¬5) ومقاتل (¬6): الزفير أول نهيق الحمار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya places zafīr in the throat and shahīq in the chest, adducing Ruʾba's line about a sound in the chest.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r6.anchor: وقال أبو العالية (¬1): الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls zafīr the loud sound and shahīq the faint sound; al-Wāḥidī says this is close to the lexicographers' and exegetes' account.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r7.anchor: وكلام ابن عباس قريب مما قاله أهل اللغة والمفسرون، فإنه قال (¬4): الزفير الصوت الشديد، والشهيق الصوت الضعيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r8.speaker: ابن عباس (رواية عطاء)
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r8.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the sounds as regret, loud breathing, and unending crying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p554/r8.anchor: ابن عباس قريب مما قاله أهل اللغة والمفسرون، فإنه قال (¬4): الزفير الصوت الشديد، والشهيق الصوت الضعيف. وقال في رواية عطاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r4.claim: The wretched make sounds of distress; zafir is the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahīq its end as it returns in the throat.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r4.anchor: { فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق } وهما من أصوات المكروبين والمحزونين، والزفير مثل أول نهيق الحمار، والشهيق آخره إذا ردده في الجوف.

ELMALILI:11:106/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r1.claim: In medical terminology, zafīr means inhaling and shahīq means exhaling.

ELMALILI:11:106/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r2.claim: In the original lexical sense, zafīr is drawing breath in deeply and then letting it out, like a distressed person's sigh.
ELMALILI:11:106/r2.anchor: asl-ı lügatta “zefîr” soluğu uzun uzadıya içeri çektikten sonra dışarı vermektir

ELMALILI:11:106/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r3.claim: Shahīq is a sob while crying, caused by intense grief; children's crying can sound this way.
ELMALILI:11:106/r3.anchor: “Şehîk” de ağlarken hıçkırmaktır ki fazla teessürden neş’et eder. Ve çocukların ağlaması öyle olur.

ELMALILI:11:106/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r4.claim: The opening and ending of a donkey's bray are also called zafīr and shahīq respectively, one inhalation and one exhalation.
ELMALILI:11:106/r4.anchor: eşeğin anırmasının evveline “zefîr”, âhirine “şehîk” denilir ki biri idhâl biri ihrâcdır.

ELMALILI:11:106/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r5.claim: In ordinary Arabic usage these are not ordinary breaths but breathing out and in with a sound of distress.
ELMALILI:11:106/r5.anchor: “zefîr” ve “şehîk” alelâde nefes alıp verme değil, ıztıraplı bir sesle nefes verip almadır.

ELMALILI:11:106/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r6.claim: The indefinite forms of zafīr and shahīq intensify the horror: these are ghastly, unprecedented gasps and sobs.
ELMALILI:11:106/r6.anchor: “zefîr ve şehîk”teki tenvinler tenkir ve tehvil içindir ki şu demek olur: Fecî bir soluk verip almaları, solurken göğüs geçirip hıçkırmaları vardır

ELMALILI:11:106/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r7.speaker: حسن
ELMALILI:11:106/r7.claim: A meaning transmitted from Hasan takes zafīr as the rising blaze of Hell, which swells until its inhabitants seem near the top before angels strike them back down.
ELMALILI:11:106/r7.anchor: Hasan’dan naklolunan bir mânaya göre “zefîr” leheb-i cehennemin irtifâ‘ıdır.

ELMALILI:11:106/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r8.claim: He relates the attempted escape and forced return to 32:20, where those trying to leave Hell are sent back into it.
ELMALILI:11:106/r8.anchor: كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓا۟ أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَآ أُعِيدُوا۟ فِيهَا

ELMALILI:11:106/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:106/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:106/r9.claim: On Hasan's reading, the fire's swelling and rising is zafīr, and its plunging back down is shahīq; the damned repeatedly rise and fall within it.
ELMALILI:11:106/r9.anchor: nâr-ı cehennemin köpürüp kabarmasıyla irtifâ‘ları zefîr, inhitatları şehîktir. Ateş içinde böyle çıkıp inip duracaklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.claim: These verses explain the gathering described in 11:103 and portray the Last Day by showing people's outcomes and destinations according to worldly faith and deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.anchor: Bu âyetler, 103. âyetin “O gün bütün insanların bir araya toplandığı gündür” meâlindeki bölümünü açıklayıcı mahiyette olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.claim: People will be divided in the afterlife into the wretched and the happy according to their faith and deeds in this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.anchor: İnsanlar, dünyadaki iman ve amellerine göre âhirette bedbahtlar ve mutlular olmak üzere iki gruba ayrılacaklardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r5.claim: Those who persisted in unbelief will be punished with Hellfire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r5.anchor: 106. âyette dünyada inkârcılıkta ısrar eden bedbahtların âhirette cehennem ateşiyle cezalandırılacakları

BURHAN:v3p48#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p48#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p48#2/r1.claim: An exception restated in a general statement and then in its detail adds emphasis: it first places the exception within the group, then distinguishes it.
BURHAN:v3p48#2/r1.anchor: ووجه التأكيد فيه أنه ثنى ذكره مرتين مرة في الجملة ومرة في التفصيل

NAHHAS:v2p302/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p302/r2.claim: The clause describing those who were wretched is a subject-predicate construction, with ففي النار as the predicate and لهم فيها زفير وشهيق continuing it.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r2.anchor: ابتداء ( ففي النار ) في موضع الخبر وكذا ( لهم فيها زفير وشهيق )

NAHHAS:v2p302/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
NAHHAS:v2p302/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliyah says zafīr comes from the chest.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r3.anchor: قال أبو العالية الزفير من الصدر والشهيق من الحلق

NAHHAS:v2p302/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
NAHHAS:v2p302/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliyah says shahīq comes from the throat.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r4.anchor: قال أبو العالية الزفير من الصدر والشهيق من الحلق

NAHHAS:v2p302/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p302/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq glosses zafīr as intense, ugly groaning and shahīq as very loud groaning.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الزفير من شديد الأنين وقبيحه والشهيق من الأنين المرتفع جدا

NAHHAS:v2p302/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r6.speaker: أهل اللغة من البصريين والكوفيين
NAHHAS:v2p302/r6.claim: Basran and Kufan linguists compare zafīr to the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahīq to its final sound.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r6.anchor: وزعم أهل اللغة من البصريين والكوفيين أن الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار في النهيق والشهيق بمنزلة آخر صوت الحمار

ITQAN:v2p314#2/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p314#2/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p314#2/r18.claim: Shahīq is a faint or weak sound.

BURHAN:v4p242/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p242/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p242/r1.claim: أما can elaborate a summary, as when the fates of two groups detail that people are gathered; it can also restrict an assertion to one claimed attribute.
BURHAN:v4p242/r1.anchor: وتذكر لتفصيل ما أجمله المخاطب وللاقتصار على بعض ما ادعى
